Abstract:
We theoretically investigate the spontaneous emission process of an atom with strong atom-field interaction in the presence of dissipation and decoherence. The reduced density matrix of the atom is governed by a stochastic quantum master equation. By using Monte Carlo wave function method, we calculate the populations and transition moments of the two states of the atom for two different initial state of the atom, the vacuum state and the coherent state, respectively, and compare with the results of the conventional quantum master equation. It is found that the atom's transition moments can reach the steady state through stochastic jumping between excited and ground states while the conventional quantum master equation does not describe the jump process. Moreover, the decoherence of the atom can be reduced by the spontaneous emission process in dissipative systems.

Abstract:
Based on the density matrix approach and the Langevin equation, the dynamics of a single electron spin in an electric field in the presence of an environment has been studied in this paper. We show that the environment effect makes the decoherence induced by the interaction with the electric field and the environment more intense. Moreover, the relation between the time for decoherence to become complete and the environmental temperature is obtained, and the influence of various temperature on the decoherence is discussed. In addition, the influence of the temperature on the populations and the coherence properties of the system are obtained through the analysis of the diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix.

Abstract:
A high-resolution model was employed for the analysis of nonlinear wave-current interaction in the nearshore. A numerical method was developed to solve the time-dependent coupled nonlinear shallow-water equations for long waves with the full linear dispersion relation. The numerical model was validated by a series of laboratory experiments. The results showed that the wave propagation was dominated by nonlinearity and the presence of a longshore current. The interaction between waves and current had complex characteristics in the wave field including refraction, reflection, interference, and diffraction. The wave energy was redistributed from high frequencies to low frequencies, which may have a negative impact on wave energy harvesting. In order to quantify the effect of the longshore current on the wave energy, a new parameter based on the phase speed and wave group velocity was introduced and analyzed. The interaction between waves and current can be evaluated by the new parameter, which can be used to predict the power harvested by a wave energy converter under the nonlinear wave-current interaction.

Abstract:
A high-resolution model was employed for the analysis of nonlinear wave-current interaction in the nearshore. A numerical method was developed to solve the time-dependent coupled nonlinear shallow-water equations for long waves with the full linear dispersion relation. The numerical model was validated by a series of laboratory experiments. The results showed that the wave propagation was dominated by nonlinearity and the presence of a longshore current. The interaction between waves and current had complex characteristics in the wave field including refraction, reflection, interference, and diffraction. The wave energy was redistributed from high frequencies to low frequencies, which may have a negative impact on wave energy harvesting. In order to quantify the effect of the longshore current on the wave energy, a new parameter based on the phase speed and wave group velocity was introduced and analyzed. The interaction between waves and current can be evaluated by the new parameter, which can be used to predict the power harvested by a wave energy converter under the nonlinear wave-current interaction.

1. Introduction

In modern electrical power systems, the loads are connected with a variety of nonlinear load models that consist of rectifier loads, adjustable speed drives and cycloconverters. Such loads cause a number of problems in power systems. Voltage and current harmonics, power quality problems, increase of system losses, etc., are some of them.

The voltage harmonics cause undesired current harmonics in the power system. This causes additional load on the system and also over-heating of the power cables. Voltage harmonics also lead to distortion of the voltage profile which cause flicker and reduction of the output of the power plant.

The shunt active power filter has been widely used to improve the power quality of the grid system [1]. The SAPF can be employed in rectifier systems, induction/synchronous motor drives and other applications which involve nonlinear loads [2]. The SAPF has a reactive power compensation capability and can be used to supply the reactive power which is required by the power system. Besides, the SAPF can be employed to compensate the voltage harmonics in order to prevent the problems associated with the harmonics. Hence, the SAPF can be employed for both harmonic compensation and reactive power compensation [2].
